constraints.interface_contract: evidence_for(executor_ids, task_class, *, economics=None, root=STATE) -> {id: {cost_to_accepted_usd, first_pass_p, expected_rework_usd, n}} from executor_economics(by='class') tuple keys; choose(task, eligible_ids, *, baseline, priority, ready_priorities: list[float], evidence, durations: dict[executor_id, float]|None = None, cfg=None) -> {executor, mode, reason, candidates, rejected, baseline, would_pick}; record(task_id, result) writes decision_log kind allocation; config [allocation] mode off|shadow|active default shadow, min_samples 5, latency_weight_usd_per_hour 2.0, critical_factor 1.0, non_critical_factor 0.25; must not import daemon or executor

spec_review_risks.issue: All six acceptance-criteria tests already pass against the current task/T-0634 worktree (ce01be3, 'T-0634 add critical-path-aware executor allocation'). orchestrator/allocation.py and tests/test_allocation.py already exist, implement evidence_for/choose/record exactly as described, and `python3 -m unittest tests.test_allocation` is green. There is nothing in scope left to fix.

The attached tests-green failure log cites test_hooks.py::test_loop_guard, test_hooks.py::test_retrospect_and_uncommitted, and test_memory_skill.py::test_recall_goal_flag_ranks/test_record_then_recall — none of which are in scope (orchestrator/allocation.py, tests/test_allocation.py) and none of which match any listed acceptance criterion. Re-running those two files directly in this worktree also passes cleanly (23/23), so the failure looks like stale/cross-run state bleed (loop_guard and retrospect counts off by exactly 2, a classic shared-STATE-dir test-isolation symptom), not a defect an allocation.py change could fix.
Head SHA is recorded as 'unknown', consistent with this failure snapshot not being reliably tied to the commit under review.
